A 181 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, since the karst fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 33 dollars per alias.
